data.title: Adani Energy Solutions’ transmission capex rises to ₹91,500 crore with Bihar project
data.description:
Adani Energy Solutions has won a transmission project in Bihar to evacuate power from an upcoming 2,400-MW power plant in Pirpainti, adding to its growing transmission portfolio.

The project, awarded through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism, is expected to generate an annual tariff of around ₹500 crore once commissioned. It will be implemented through a special purpose vehicle (SPV), Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd., and is scheduled for delivery by the last quarter of 2028.

The project will support the evacuation of power from the 3X800 MW Pirpainti thermal power plant while strengthening Bihar’s transmission network and improving supply reliability.

“The Pirpainti transmission scheme will create a robust evacuation system for 2,400 MW of generation capacity while strengthening Bihar’s transmission backbone. It will enhance grid reliability and resilience and help the state meet its growing power demand,” said Kandarp Patel, CEO of Adani Energy Solutions.

881 circuit km of lines, 3,160 MVA capacity

The project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to the company’s portfolio. Once completed, Adani Energy Solutions’ transmission network will expand to 30,683 ckm, with transformation capacity reaching 146,585 MVA.

The infrastructure will include four gas-insulated substations (GIS) at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation capacity.

It will also involve the construction of 400 kV double-circuit lines connecting Pirpainti with Jhanjharpur and Begusarai, and Begusarai with Bakhtiyarpur. Two 220 kV double-circuit lines will connect Jhanjharpur with Bethauli and Begusarai with Begusarai Town.

The project also includes the loop-in-loop-out (LILO) of existing 220 kV and 132 kV transmission lines at Jhanjharpur, and the construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur GSS.

With the addition of the Bihar project, Adani Energy Solutions’ transmission capex now stands at around ₹91,500 crore.

Shares of Adani Energy Solutions were trading at ₹1,477 on the BSE at 2:51 pm on Wednesday, November 19, down ₹1, or 0.068%, from the previous close.

data.title: South Africa's Investec reports 8.4% rise in half-year earnings
data.description:
By Nqobile Dludla

Investec reported an 8.4% rise in half-year headline earnings on Thursday, supported by revenue growth as it increased its average lending book and client base as the South African bank expands its business among private banking customers and mid-sized corporates.

  • Investec, which also operates in Britain, posted headline earnings per share of 39.8 pence for the six months ended September 30, compared with 36.7 pence in the previous year

  • Adjusted operating profit grew 5.6% to £494.5 million ($649.48 million)

  • Revenue increased 6.7% to £1.16 billion as net interest income rose 6.7% to £715 million, while non-interest revenue grew 6.7% to £454.8 million

  • Net core loans rose 10.5% to £37.4 billion, reflecting strong growth across private banking and corporate lending books in South Africa and the UK

  • Growth in NII was partly offset by the "negative endowment" effect of declining global interest rates and margin pressure due to highly competitive pricing across its operating countries, the lender said

  • The credit loss ratio - a measure of bad loans against total lending - on core loans improved to 28 basis points, as credit loss impairment charges decreased to £51.2 million

  • It announced an interim dividend of 18.5 pence per share

($1 = 0.7614 pounds)

data.title: Treasury, Eurozone Bond Yields Edge Higher — Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields turned higher in European trade on Thursday as the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a faster pace.

Eurozone bond yields were slightly higher ahead of heavy bond supply from Spain and France. Spain will auction 4.5 billion euros to 5.5 billion euros ($4.94 billion to $6.04 billion) in three bonds, including a new seven-year one. France will offer a combined 11.25 billion euros to 13.75 billion euros in a total of eight nominal and inflation-linked bonds.

The 10-year Treasury yield last traded 1.9 basis points higher at 5.084%, while 10-year German Bund yield edged up 0.9 basis points to 3.380%, according to Tradeweb.

"Ten-year Bund yields remain within their recently established range just below 3.4%, but volatility is picking up amid hawkish central bank talk and shaky risk sentiment," said Hauke Siemssen, rates strategist at Commerzbank, in a note.

Minutes of the latest Fed rate-setting meeting, where the Fed left interest rates unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase of half a percentage point in December. The committee's discussion of inflation revealed increasing concern of broadening price pressure amid strong growth in economic activity, Stuart Paul, U.S. economist at UBS, said in a note.

The minutes increased market expectations of a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike at the December meeting. Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and an 8% likelihood of a 50-basis-point tightening, according to LSEG. A 50-basis-point hike was priced with a 2% probability on Wednesday.

"An unyielding Federal Reserve continues to govern fixed income and currency markets," Patrick Munnelly, market strategist at Tickmill Group, said in a note. "Wednesday's October [Federal Open Market Committee] minutes confirmed that nearly all officials anticipate further rate hikes to return inflation to target, with two participants even floating the risk of a 50bps move in December if price pressures persist," he said.

Crucially, policymakers took comfort from tighter market-implied rate paths doing the Fed's heavy lifting--meaning any sustained AI-driven easing in financial conditions risks provoking a sharper monetary pushback, Munnelly added.

The Treasury will conduct a $19 billion auction of 10-year Treasury inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, on Thursday.

Despite the backdrop of higher real yields, cheap valuations, and improving liquidity, J.P. Morgan analysts think the hawkish Fed backdrop and amount of supply in the 10-year sector means the auction "will need more of a concession to be digested smoothly."

data.title: UniCredit Strikes Deal With Germany to Clear Path for Commerzbank Takeover
data.description:
By Michael Hennessey

UniCredit reached an agreement with the German government to resolve key issues in the takeover of Commerzbank, clearing the way for the Italian lender to take control of Germany's second-largest listed bank.

To meet Germany's demands, UniCredit agreed to keep Commerzbank's headquarters in Frankfurt, where the bank will remain listed on the stock exchange, according to a letter from UniCredit Chief Executive Officer Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil.

As a concession to UniCredit, Germany will no longer seek to directly nominate members for Commerzbank's supervisory board. In turn, to maintain good relations with Berlin, UniCredit said it has secured government approval for two independent candidates it plans to nominate instead.

Orcel said in a statement that the support from Germany for a "swift handover" will "help provide clarity and momentum for the next phase to the betterment of both Commerzbank's clients and employees."

"We look forward to continuing this constructive engagement with the minister and all remaining stakeholders as we resolve any outstanding questions and, in turn, realize the significant potential of Commerzbank as part of the UniCredit Group," Orcel added.

Commerzbank said in a statement that it welcomed the commitments announced by UniCredit.

"Key decisions will continue to be made in Germany. Employee rights and existing agreements are also explicitly recognized," the German bank said.

Commerzbank said its board would work with UniCredit to build on the strengths of both banks.

UniCredit started building its stake in Commerzbank in September 2024 and has since continued to increase its ownership to just under 50%.

Commerzbank is currently valued at around 41 billion euros ($45 billion), meaning a takeover would rank as Europe's biggest banking deals since the 2008-9 financial crisis.

The European Commission, the executive arm of the European Union, approved the deal earlier this week and said it wouldn't raise competition concerns in the bloc. The European Central Bank approved the deal in October.

UniCredit is now waiting for final regulatory approvals, which it expects to receive by the end of November, to allow it to take control of the bank.

The Italian bank said last week that new governance arrangements and the implementation of its strategy for Commerzbank are expected by the first quarter of 2027.

(09:28 GMT) Kuaishou Swings to Quarterly Loss as AI Spending Intensifies

By Kimberley Kao

Chinese short-video company Kuaishou Technology warned of continued headwinds as it swung to a loss in the third quarter, dragged by increased spending on its artificial-intelligence business.

The Beijing-based company on Thursday reported a net loss of 959 million yuan, equivalent to $143.8 million, for the three months ended September.

That missed the 163.2 million yuan loss expected by analysts in a Visible Alpha poll. Adjusting for share-based compensation expenses, net fair-value changes on investments and finance costs on redemption financial liabilities, net profit fell 84%, Kuaishou said.

The business was affected by intense external competition and a changing consumer environment, it said.

Like its Chinese tech peers, Kuaishou, one of China's largest short-video platform, has been spending big on AI as industry competition heats up.

Revenue fell 11% from a year earlier to 31.59 billion yuan, slightly missing market expectations of 32.94 billion yuan.

Kuaishou's other services segment, which includes Kling AI, posted revenue growth of 1.5% for the third quarter, as higher revenue from games and Kling AI offset a decline in e-commerce revenue.

That compared with an 11% decline in revenue from online marketing services, and a 19% drop in revenue from its live-streaming business.

"The near-term operating environment remains challenging, with relatively conservative consumers' and marketers' spending sentiments and intense competition," the company said.

Kuaishou said it expects its Kling investments and broader AI strategy to weigh on profitability in the near term. Revenue and profits may remain under pressure in the fourth quarter, it said.

data.title: Japan Tobacco to Book $8.6 Billion Loss on Russia Business — Update
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

Japan Tobacco expects to book an $8.6 billion loss, cut dividends and reduce executive pay after losing control of its Russian business.

The Japanese tobacco maker said Thursday that it can no longer make business decisions concerning its Russian operations as it did previously and would record a special loss of 1.377 trillion yen related to the loss of control.

Earlier this month, Japan Tobacco said all seven of its Russian entities had been placed under temporary administration by a Russian company on the orders of President Vladimir Putin.

The move marked an escalation in Russian measures against Japanese businesses following Tokyo's support for Ukraine and its participation in Western sanctions against Moscow over its 2022 invasion.

Japan Tobacco on Thursday projected a net loss of Y724.00 billion, equivalent to $4.54 billion, for 2026, primarily due to the special loss related to its Russian business.

The company said excluding its Russian entities from consolidated financial reporting doesn't mean it is relinquishing or selling legal ownership of the businesses or withdrawing from Russia.

Japan Tobacco cut its dividend forecast for this year to Y204 a share from Y272 but said it remains confident it can raise dividends in the coming years, supported by profit growth.

The company's Russian operations had about Y1.5 trillion in assets, including goodwill and roughly Y360 billion in cash and deposits, as well as about Y200 billion in liabilities at the end of September.

Japan Tobacco had expected Russia to account for about 10% of its revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit in 2026.

The company, formerly a state-owned monopoly, was just under 38% owned by the Japanese government at the end of 2025.

Japan Tobacco, whose brands include Winston and Camel, is one of Russia's largest tobacco companies, with a market share of nearly 40%.

The company said it aims to maintain its Russian operations while prioritizing employee safety and will take all available measures to protect its business rights and assets.

Its board also decided to halve the monthly base pay of five directors, including Chairman Shigeaki Okamoto and Chief Executive Takehiko Tsutsui, for two months. Tsutsui and two other representative directors will also forgo their executive bonuses this year.

Oil prices were supported by lingering supply risks as the US-Iran conflict dragged on on Thursday.

Iran's navy said three oil tankers sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.

On Thursday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, but the Saudi Civil Defense agency said the danger had passed.

In the spot market, Taiwan's CPC Corporation and Japan's Taiyo Oil bought US crude this week for delivery in February, multiple trade sources in the market said.

Iraq's state oil marketer SOMO has offered December-loading Basrah crude cargoes at discounts of up to $33 a barrel to destination market benchmarks, according to an offer document reviewed by Reuters.

data.title: Vale Indonesia says it will raise nickel matte output to 73,000 metric tons in 2027
data.description:
Nickel miner PT Vale Indonesia will aim to produce around 73,000 metric tons of nickel matte in 2027 as it plans to ramp up its Sorowako smelter to full capacity, according to a company presentation on Thursday.

  • The outlook was presented to analysts in a gathering on Thursday, Vale Indonesia said in a statement

  • Vale expects to produce 67,645 tons of nickel matte this year

  • In the first nine months of 2026, Vale's nickel matte production was 48,114 tons, down from 54,975 tons in the same period last year, company data showed

  • Vale also plans to spend $1.04 billion in capital expenditure next year, including $556 million on the smelters currently being built by its joint ventures

data.title: Joyy's Likely to Continue Solid Momentum Into Next Year — Market Talk
data.description: Joyy's business is likely to carry solid momentum into next year, according to Jefferies analysts in a research note. The Chinese social media company's revenue exceeded consensus in 3Q, they say. Total revenue is expected maintain solid growth in 2027, with its social entertainment unit recording a healthy cash flow, the analysts say, citing management's remarks. Jefferies keeps a buy rating, and raises its target price of its ADRs to $90.70 from $87.00. Its ADRs were last traded at US$78.48. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
